⚖️ TITLE DUE DILIGENCE | THE “13-YEAR RULE” — A COMMON MISUNDERSTANDING IN BANKING & NBFC LENDING

In property-backed lending, one phrase is heard repeatedly: “The property has a 13-year title search, so the title is clear.”

But from a legal due-diligence perspective, this statement requires a much closer examination.

👉 13 years is not, by itself, a statutory certificate of clear and marketable title.

For Banks, NBFCs and HFCs, the search period is an important part of the credit-risk framework. But title due diligence is much broader than counting years.
What should an NBFC/Bank actually ask?

Before accepting an immovable property as security, the legal review should examine:
🔹 Root of title
🔹 Complete chain of title
🔹 Sale/Transfer/Partition/Gift/Release documents
🔹 Inheritance and succession issues
🔹 Encumbrances and prior mortgages
🔹 CERSAI records
🔹 Revenue & mutation records
🔹 Pending litigation and court records
🔹 Acquisition/land-use restrictions
🔹 Possession and identification of the property
🔹 Authority and capacity of the transferor
🔹 Original title documents
🔹 Registration and execution of documents
🔹 Existing charge/NOC/release documents

RBI itself has highlighted the importance of verification of title and periodic legal audit of title documents, particularly because defective or fabricated title documents and multiple financing against the same security remain significant risks.

The real issue is this:13 YEARS ≠ CLEAR TITLE

A 13-year search may satisfy an institution's internal policy for a particular category of loan, but it cannot automatically eliminate a defect originating before that period.

For example: 2018 → Sale Deed → 2026 → Mortgage

If the 2018 seller's title itself originated from a defective partition, inheritance, forged document or incomplete chain, merely searching 2013–2026 may not answer the fundamental question:
“How did this person acquire a valid title in the first place?”

For NBFCs, this distinction is critical.An NBFC does not merely need a property that appears transferable.

It needs security that is:
VALID + MARKETABLE + ENFORCEABLE + TRACEABLE

Because the real test of a title opinion often begins when the account becomes an NPA and enforcement is required.

RBI's current framework also emphasizes legal audit/re-verification of title documents for certain NBFC credit facilities, demonstrating that title verification is an ongoing risk-control function—not merely a one-time formality.

comment: A key risk often appears when title diligence focuses on documents rather than the people and transactions behind them. Verifying execution capacity, succession rights and historical transfers can prevent issues that surface only during enforcement.
